source.title: AWS Bedrock Chat Model: real token usage is never read, and completion tokens are recorded as 0 when Claude extended thinking is enabled

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

The AWS Bedrock Chat Model node (`@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatAwsBedrock`, uses `ChatBedrockConverse` from `@langchain/aws`) never records the real token usage returned by Bedrock. It always falls back to `tokenUsageEstimate`.

On top of that, when the model returns extended-thinking content (e.g. Claude Haiku 5.5, where adaptive thinking is on by default), the estimate for `completionTokens` is always `0`, so the output tokens disappear from the execution data entirely.

We bill our customers from the token usage stored in the execution data, so this makes per-execution cost tracking impossible for Bedrock + thinking, and only approximate (tokenizer estimate) for Bedrock without thinking.

Root cause, as far as I can tell (same code in 2.45.6, 2.46.7, 2.47.3 and master):

1. `N8nLlmTracing` (`packages/@n8n/ai-utilities/src/utils/n8n-llm-tracing.ts`) uses the default `tokensUsageParser`, which only reads `result.llmOutput.tokenUsage`. `ChatBedrockConverse` reports usage on the message (`generation.message.usage_metadata` → `input_tokens` / `output_tokens`), not in `llmOutput.tokenUsage`, so the parser always returns `completionTokens: 0` and the node falls back to the estimate. `LmChatAwsBedrock.node.ts` instantiates `new N8nLlmTracing(this)` without a provider-specific parser.
2. The estimate is computed from `generation.text`. When the response content is an array of blocks (`reasoning_content` + `text`), `generation.text` is `""` (also visible in the stored run data: `response.generations[0][0].text === ""`), so `estimateTokensFromGeneration` returns `0`.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Basic LLM Chain (with or without Structured Output Parser) connected to an AWS Bedrock Chat Model node.
2. Model: `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` (thinking enabled by default), no `additionalModelRequestFields`.
3. Execute the workflow.
4. Inspect the AWS Bedrock Chat Model output in the execution data:
   - `tokenUsageEstimate.completionTokens` is `0`
   - `response.generations[0][0].text` is `""` even though the chain received a valid answer
   - no `tokenUsage` (real usage) is present
5. Now set `additionalModelRequestFields` to `{"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}` and execute again: `completionTokens` is now > 0, but it is still only `tokenUsageEstimate`, never the real `usage_metadata` returned by Bedrock.

### Expected behavior

- The Bedrock node records the real usage returned by Bedrock (`usage_metadata.input_tokens` / `output_tokens`) as `tokenUsage`, like other providers that populate `llmOutput.tokenUsage`.
- When only an estimate is possible, text content blocks are considered (not only `generation.text`), so the completion estimate is not `0` for responses that contain reasoning blocks.

Possible fix: pass a `tokensUsageParser` in `LmChatAwsBedrock.node.ts` that falls back to `generations[0][0].message.usage_metadata` when `llmOutput.tokenUsage` is missing (the default parser could also do this generically for all chat models).

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `N8nLlmTracing` and Bedrock node source. Bedrock still constructs the tracer without a provider-specific `tokensUsageParser`, and the default parser reads only `llmOutput.tokenUsage`; the reported `message.usage_metadata` therefore is not consumed here. The fallback estimator also maps each generation to `g.text`, so an array-content response with an empty `text` field would estimate zero completion tokens. A Bedrock parser for the message usage metadata plus estimation from text content blocks (when needed) would address these two distinct paths.
